bull.b: Validated proteoform resolution and reproducibility support the platform’s scientific credibility and potential differentiation in proteomics. These results can improve customer confidence, strengthen future assay development, and provide a durable foundation for partnerships and commercial adoption.

Concentrating application R&D on proteoforms creates a clearer product strategy and commercialization path. Planned assays, early access, and staged instrument shipments provide multiple milestones that could convert technical progress into recurring consumable and software revenue over time.

Lower operating expenses and a modestly improved net loss show management is adjusting spending while continuing platform development. Sustained cost discipline can extend financial runway, preserve resources for priority proteoform programs, and reduce the pace of cash consumption.

bear.b: Revenue remains extremely small relative to operating costs, indicating that commercialization has not yet reached meaningful scale. Persistent operating and net losses limit internal funding capacity and leave future performance highly dependent on successful customer conversion and product launches.

Deeply negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is still funding operations primarily through its cash balance and external capital. Continued consumption may require financing before profitability, creating dilution or borrowing risk and constraining strategic flexibility.

The broadscale delay postpones a potentially important application of the platform and extends the period before it can contribute to commercial adoption. Additional probe, model, and assay work increases execution uncertainty while management reallocates resources toward narrower proteoform opportunities.
